summary:
LUNA-LINK is an interactive lunar mission-planning platform designed to simplify the complex relationship between lunar illumination, Earth visibility, and lander operations. We developed a unified application featuring SunTrack, a 3D lunar sunlight simulator; EarthLink, a communication-window calendar; and LUNA-RESCUE, an interactive lander energy-survival simulator. Additional features include an interactive landing-site explorer with custom coordinates and site comparisons, mission timeline replays, educational mission challenges, and downloadable mission reports. With Explorer and Mission Control modes, the platform caters to both the general public and any user seeking more technical insights.

LUNA-LINK addresses the challenge by allowing users to investigate how landing location and mission timing influence sunlight availability, solar-energy generation, and communication opportunities. By combining visualizations, astronomical calculations, and hypothetical mission simulations, it makes these interconnected constraints easier to understand and evaluate. Its modular architecture is also designed to accommodate future NASA datasets as they become available.

Ultimately, LUNA-LINK promotes accessible space-science education while demonstrating how scientific data can support more informed lunar mission planning.
details:
LUNA-LINK is an interactive lunar mission-planning and survival platform that demonstrates how sunlight availability, Earth visibility and energy management influence lunar lander operations. It works by allowing users to select from curated lunar landing locations or enter custom coordinates, choose mission dates and times, and explore how environmental conditions change throughout a mission.

The platform integrates several interconnected features. SunTrack provides a 3D visualisation of lunar illumination, solar elevation and potential sunlight periods. EarthLink displays predicted direct-to-Earth visibility windows through an interactive communication calendar. LUNA-RESCUE simulates a hypothetical lander's energy consumption, solar-energy generation and battery levels under changing environmental conditions. Users can also compare landing sites, replay mission timelines, participate in interactive mission challenges and generate mission reports. The application offers Explorer Mode for beginners and Mission Control Mode for users interested in more detailed technical information.

The primary benefit of LUNA-LINK is that it brings several interconnected aspects of lunar mission planning into one accessible platform. Rather than examining illumination, communication and power management independently, users can understand how changes in one environmental factor can affect the entire mission. This encourages scientific curiosity, practical problem-solving and a deeper understanding of the engineering challenges involved in lunar exploration.

Our intended impact is to make complex space-science concepts accessible to students and the general public while demonstrating how scientific data can support engineering decisions. We also designed the platform with a modular data architecture so that additional official NASA datasets can be integrated as they become available. Scientific observations, calculated predictions and illustrative simulation values are clearly distinguished to maintain transparency.

The application is being developed as a browser-based web platform using Python, JavaScript, HTML and CSS with AI assisting the development process. Technologies such as Three.js support 3D visualization, while charting libraries can be used for timelines and energy graphs. Publicly available scientific resources, including NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter datasets, JPL Horizons and the SPICE Toolkit, inform the scientific approach. No specialized physical hardware is required.

What makes LUNA-LINK creative is its integration of astronomical visualization, interactive engineering simulations and educational challenges into a single experience. Our team considered scientific accuracy, accessibility, usability, computational limitations, data availability and future scalability. We also prioritized building a functional and understandable platform rather than presenting complex scientific information without context.

Ultimately, LUNA-LINK aims to transform lunar mission planning from something users simply read about into something they can actively explore, experiment with and understand.
